dates.note: no generation timestamp is recorded: this file must be byte-reproducible, and the build time is the commit time

grader_runner_coverage.foundry: implemented in scripts/prove_grader.py (forge build + forge test)
grader_runner_coverage.hardhat: NOT implemented — the task is recorded, its two-side evidence is cited, and the grader refuses to credit a stage it cannot run

grader_self_check.validates: the grader's stage rules against this project's own recorded runs

isolation.answer_key_location: outside the repository; see commitment hashes below
model_must_not_see: any answer key or hidden test

criteria: no fixed revision appears in any model-facing file
no harness source or expected assertion appears in a public file
tasks sharing one repository are reported as a single group so a split cannot be called project-held-out
leakage_audit.statement: this split is leakage-audited under the criteria above; it is not and must not be described as contamination-proof

notes: the reason a recorded test failed now comes from the `forge --json` entry (scripts/experiments.py:per_test_reason); the recorder used to read only the human `[FAIL: …]` line, which does not exist under `--json`, so every recorded run stored `reason: null`. Already-recorded artefacts are evidence and are not rewritten — the self-check above recovers the reason by replaying the preserved stdout through the grader's own parser, and future runs record it directly.
4 of 7 recorded runs had their failure reason recovered from the artefact bytes rather than the summary.

pool.why_smaller: the pool is bounded by the two-revision evidence that exists in this tree: seven executed vulnerable/fixed pairs in the v1 layer plus one hardhat two-side run in the V3.2 layer. Every additional task needs a pinned fixed revision and a test that was actually run on both sides, so the private split is recorded at its real size rather than padded to 200.

private_commitment.location: outside the repository (path deliberately not published)
private_commitment.note: publish this commitment before a run so that a later comparison shows whether the answer key moved; the key itself stays out of the repo

stage_rules.compiles: the toolchain build succeeded; a compile or dependency failure stops the run at this stage and never counts as a failed proof
stage_rules.executes: forge (or hardhat) ran at least one test from the submission
stage_rules.generated: the submission contains at least one non-empty test file
stage_rules.impact_reproduced: on the vulnerable revision the expected test failed with the expected assertion signature, not an unrelated error
stage_rules.patch_verified: the same test file, unmodified, passed on the second revision
